observed_scene: Boundary edits for a D-FINE detection on the Instance-RSDD reserve. Independent selection adds four native cells and removes four. \CaseCaption{The GT polygon, native mask and edited mask are pooled on an \(8\times8\) display grid, with coverage rounded to the nearest quarter. Continuous IoU rises from 51.71 to 51.92 points on the native geometry.}{The left panel shows the SAR crop, the inset enlarges the corresponding native mask cells, and the right panel shows the edited mask. The dashed outline is the annotated polygon.} Polygon--cell fractions supervise the scalar ROH during fitting.
observed_sampling: Native boundary support. Within the box \(B\), the writer takes candidate additions from the outer two rings and removals from the inner two rings. Candidates on each side are ordered by \(\lvert p_i-0.5\rvert\) and capped at 32. \CaseCaption{The top panels use a schematic mask, box and scores. The lower panel shows a D-FINE native mask on the Instance-RSDD reserve, pooled into \(8\times8\) display bins and rounded to quarter occupancy. Its native continuous IoU is 51.71 points.}{The left panel shows the observed D-FINE mask on the Instance-RSDD reserve. The displayed box and score ordering illustrate the sampling rule.}
observed_readout: Target and decoder response for the scalar ROH. \CaseCaption{At left, the Instance-RSDD reference polygon is pooled into an \(8\times8\) display grid with quarter-occupancy levels.}{At left, the annotated outline is overlaid on the Instance-RSDD SAR crop.} The other panels illustrate one native cell. The polygon covers half of this example cell (\(q_i=0.50\)). Bilinear interpolation of four decoder neighbors gives \(p_i\) at the same cell center.
observed_placement: Equal-count endpoint placement. In the upper schematic, \(F\), \(L\) and \(I\) each add and remove two cells. \(F\) sets the maximum retained edge length \(\rho=\sqrt{2}\) native pixels, \(L\) re-pairs cells within this cap, and \(I\) ranks each side independently. The illustrative predicted intersection gains are 0.89, 0.99 and 1.44 cell areas. Below, all three methods add and remove four cells on the same D-FINE detection from the Instance-RSDD reserve. Their continuous IoUs are 51.52, 51.73 and 51.92 points. \CaseCaption{The \(8\times8\) bins show mean GT or mask coverage.}{All panels share the SAR crop, scale and annotated outline.} The observed scores use native polygon--cell geometry.
observed_placement_loss: Matched-count placement in a loss case. The upper schematic uses two additions and two removals. The gains of 0.89, 0.99 and 1.44 are predicted intersection changes in cell areas, with \(\rho=\sqrt{2}\) native pixels. For the observed D-FINE detection below, each writer adds and removes eight cells. Continuous IoU is 67.73 for \(F\), 68.00 for \(L\) and 67.85 for \(I\), in points. \CaseCaption{The \(8\times8\) display bins average GT or mask coverage.}{The GT outline and three outputs share the Instance-RSDD SAR crop and scale.} IoU uses native geometry.
observed_allocation: Signed allocation at a fixed total. The upper schematic gives four flips to each writer on a 15-cell mask. The equal split preserves its area and three additions with one removal increase it to 17 cells. Below, the bars give the observed totals across the candidate stream for the first dual-reference ROH fit on the same 183 SSDD development images. The equal split adds and removes 57,692 cells. The variable split adds 67,777 and removes 47,607, for the same 115,384 flips.
observed_phoenix: Frozen Phoenix XL1 support and writing rules. The upper matrix keeps the fifth-iteration response fixed. Its candidate grid and counts illustrate the four combinations of sampled or full-grid support and threshold or exact-total writing. The two lower PSeg-SSDD cases compare the full-grid threshold and exact-total arms. The gain case uses 38 versus 16 flips and the loss case uses 75 versus 16. \CaseCaption{The \(8\times8\) coverage grids pool \(5\times5\) native cells per bin in the gain case and \(7\times7\) in the loss case. Coverage is rounded to the nearest quarter.}{Both outputs in a pair share their SAR crop and scale. The solid mask boundary and dashed GT polygon mark the edited and annotated hulls.} IoU for each instance uses native geometry.
